questions.stem_en: A team hosts its code in GitHub and uses an AWS CodeBuild project with a webhook to run unit tests. The tests must run when a pull request is opened and every time new commits are added to it. The tests must run only for pull requests that target the main branch. Pull requests that target other branches must not start any build. Which webhook configuration meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices_en.text: Two filter groups: one with EVENT set to PULL_REQUEST_CREATED, PULL_REQUEST_UPDATED and one with BASE_REF set to refs/heads/main.
One filter group with EVENT set to PULL_REQUEST_CREATED, PULL_REQUEST_UPDATED and BASE_REF set to refs/heads/main.
One filter group with EVENT set to PUSH, PULL_REQUEST_CREATED and BASE_REF set to refs/heads/main.
One filter group with EVENT set to PULL_REQUEST_CREATED, PULL_REQUEST_MERGED and BASE_REF set to refs/heads/main.

explanation.summary: ビルドは、どれかのフィルターグループが真になると始まり、グループが真になるのはその中の全フィルターが真の時。1 つのグループに「作成と更新の PR イベント」と「BASE_REF が main」を入れると、main 向けの PR の作成と更新だけでビルドが始まる。

per_choice.A: グループどうしはどれか 1 つが真ならよいので、PR イベントだけのグループが他のブランチ向けの PR でも真になり、ビルドが始まってしまう。
per_choice.B: 正しい。同じグループの中のフィルターは全部そろった時だけ真になるので、main 向けの PR の作成と更新に絞れる。
per_choice.C: BASE_REF は PR のイベントでしか使えない。また PR に新しいコミットを足した時（PULL_REQUEST_UPDATED）が入っていない。
per_choice.D: PR に新しいコミットを足した時（PULL_REQUEST_UPDATED）に動かない。MERGED はマージの時で、要件に無い。

references.quote: A build is triggered if any filter group evaluates to true, which occurs when all the filters in the group evaluate to true.
A BASE_REF filter can be used with pull request events only.

questions.stem_en: A company builds a .NET application with AWS CodeBuild. The test framework writes its results as NUnit 3 XML files to the test-results directory. The developers want the results to appear as a test report in CodeBuild for each build. The company does not want to add steps that convert or upload files. Which change meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices_en.text: Add a reports section to the buildspec that lists the test-results files and sets file-format to NUNIT3XML.
Add a reports section to the buildspec that lists the test-results files and leaves file-format unset.
Add a build command that converts the results to JUnit XML, and list the converted files in a reports section.
Add the test-results files to the artifacts section so that they are stored in Amazon S3 after each build.

explanation.summary: buildspec の reports に、試験結果のファイルの場所（files）と形式（file-format）を書くと、CodeBuild がテストレポートにする。file-format を書かないと JUNITXML として扱うので、NUnit 3 XML なら NUNIT3XML を指定する。

per_choice.A: 正しい。形式を NUNIT3XML にすれば、変換なしでテストレポートになる。
per_choice.B: file-format を書かないと JUNITXML として扱われ、NUnit 3 XML の形式と合わない。
per_choice.C: 動くが、変換の手順を足すことになり、要件に反する。CodeBuild は NUnit 3 XML をそのまま扱える。
per_choice.D: S3 にファイルが残るだけで、CodeBuild のテストレポートにはならない。

references.quote: Optional mapping. Represents the report file format. If not specified, JUNITXML is used.
NUNIT3XML NUnit 3 XML

questions.stem_en: A company uses an AWS CodePipeline V2 pipeline with a GitHub source action that uses a connection. The pipeline must start when a pull request that targets the main branch is opened, and again whenever a new revision is published to that pull request. The pipeline must also start for every push to main. The company wants to use one pipeline and no custom code. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices_en.text: Add a trigger with a pullRequest filter for main with the Open and Closed events, and a push filter for main.
Add a trigger with only a push filter for main, and add a CodeBuild webhook that runs tests for pull requests.
Create a second pipeline for pull request events, and keep the first pipeline for pushes to main.
Add a trigger with a pullRequest filter for main with the Open and Update events, and a push filter for main.

explanation.summary: V2 パイプラインのトリガーは、git の設定で push と pull request のイベントを絞り込める。pull request の Open は PR が作られた時、Update は PR に新しいリビジョンが出た時に動くので、main への push のフィルターと合わせると 1 つのパイプラインで要件を満たす。

per_choice.A: Closed は PR が閉じられた時。新しいリビジョンが出た時（Update）に動かない。
per_choice.B: PR の時に動くのは CodeBuild だけで、パイプラインは始まらない。
per_choice.C: 動くが、パイプラインを 1 つにする要件に反する。
per_choice.D: 正しい。Open と Update の pull request のフィルターと、main の push のフィルターを 1 つのパイプラインに入れる。

references.quote: Update - This option triggers the pipeline when a pull request revision is published for the branch/file path.
Triggers allow you to configure your pipeline to start on a particular event type or filtered event type, such as when a change on a particular branch or pull request is detected.

questions.stem_en: A company has JMeter scripts for its web application. Before each release, the company must simulate thousands of concurrent users to find bottlenecks, and must also run the same load test every week to catch performance regressions. The DevOps team does not want to provision or manage load-generating servers, and wants to add the tests to its CI/CD pipeline. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices_en.text: Run JMeter on an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances, and start the group from the pipeline before each release.
Rewrite the tests for a different framework, and run them from a developer workstation before each release.
Deploy Distributed Load Testing on AWS, use the existing JMeter scripts, schedule a weekly test, and call it from the pipeline.
Run the JMeter scripts once a week from a single shared server, and skip load tests for releases.

explanation.summary: Distributed Load Testing on AWS は、サーバーを用意せずに何千もの利用者のリクエストを流し、リリースの前にボトルネックを見つける。JMeter などのスクリプトを使え、すぐ・決めた日時・くり返しの予定で動かせる。CI/CD のパイプラインに入れる使い方も想定されている。

per_choice.A: 負荷を出すサーバーを持って管理することになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.B: 書き直す必要は無く、手元で動かすのでは自動にならない。
per_choice.C: 正しい。今の JMeter のスクリプトのまま、くり返しの予定とパイプラインの両方で使える。
per_choice.D: リリースの前の試験の要件に反し、1 台では何千もの利用者を再現しにくい。

references.quote: This solution simulates thousands of connected users generating HTTP requests at a sustained rate without the need to provision servers.
Customize your application tests using JMeter, k6, Locust test scripts, or simple HTTP endpoint configuration.
Integrate automated performance testing into continuous integration and deployment pipelines to catch performance issues early in the development cycle.
Schedules tests to run immediately, at a specific future date and time, or on a recurring schedule using cron expressions for automated regression testing.

questions.stem_en: A CodeBuild project runs 2,000 integration tests in one build, which takes 60 minutes. The team wants the same test suite, with the same configuration, to be split across 10 builds that run at the same time. The team does not want to divide the test files by hand or maintain several projects. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices_en.text: Configure a batch build with a build matrix that lists 10 configurations of the same environment.
Create 10 CodeBuild projects, and give each project a list of test files to run.
Run the tests in one build, and start the build 10 times from the pipeline at the same time.
Configure a batch build with a build fanout and set the parallelism field to 10.

explanation.summary: build fanout は、1 つの作業をバッチの中の複数のビルドに分け、試験を並べて動かすのに使える。parallelism の値に合わせて、試験のケースを分けた塊ごとに別のビルドを作る。build matrix は、違う設定の組み合わせごとにビルドを作る物。

per_choice.A: build matrix は違う設定の組み合わせごとにビルドを作る物で、同じ試験を分けて動かす物ではない。
per_choice.B: 試験のファイルを手で分け、10 個のプロジェクトを持つことになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.C: 同じ試験の全部を 10 回動かすだけで、試験は分かれない。
per_choice.D: 正しい。試験を 10 に分け、並べて動かす。

references.quote: A build fanout defines a task that will be split into multiple builds in the batch. This can be used for running tests in parallel.
CodeBuild creates a separate build for each shard of test cases based on the value set in the parallelism field.
A build matrix defines tasks with different configurations that run in parallel.

questions.stem_en: A library must be tested on three runtime versions and two operating system images, which gives six combinations. All six combinations must run in parallel for each pull request, and the team wants to define them in one place instead of maintaining separate projects. Which CodeBuild configuration meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

choices_en.text: A batch build with a build matrix that lists the runtime versions and the images.
A batch build with a build fanout and the parallelism field set to 6.
Six CodeBuild projects, one for each combination, started from the same pipeline stage.
One build that runs the six combinations one after another in the buildspec.

explanation.summary: build matrix は違う設定の作業を並べて動かす物で、CodeBuild は設定の組み合わせごとに別のビルドを作り、並べて動かす。build fanout は同じ作業の試験を塊に分ける物。

per_choice.A: 正しい。組み合わせごとにビルドが作られ、並べて動く。
per_choice.B: build fanout は同じ設定のまま試験を分ける物で、違う設定の組み合わせを作らない。
per_choice.C: 動くが、6 つのプロジェクトを持つことになり、要件に反する。
per_choice.D: 1 つのビルドで順に動かすので、並べて動かす要件に反する。

references.quote: CodeBuild creates a separate build for each possible configuration combination.
These builds run in parallel.
CodeBuild creates a separate build for each shard of test cases based on the value set in the parallelism field.

questions.stem_en: An Amazon ECS service runs a container whose health check command returns a non-zero exit code until the application finishes loading, which takes about 90 seconds. The health check uses the default interval, timeout, and retries. New tasks are marked unhealthy and replaced before they finish starting. The team wants failed checks during startup to be ignored without weakening checks afterward. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices_en.text: Set retries in the container health check to 20.
Set interval in the container health check to 400 seconds.
Set startPeriod in the container health check to 120 seconds.
Set timeout in the container health check to 90 seconds.

explanation.summary: コンテナのヘルスチェックは、コマンドの終了コード 0 で成功、0 以外で失敗とする。startPeriod は、起動の間の失敗を retries の回数に数えない猶予（0〜300 秒、既定は無効）。interval は 5〜300 秒、timeout は 2〜60 秒、retries は 1〜10 回。

per_choice.B: interval は 300 秒まで。起動の後の確かめも弱くなる。
per_choice.C: 正しい。起動の間の失敗を数えず、その後は今までどおり確かめる。
per_choice.D: timeout は 60 秒まで。1 回の確かめの待ち時間で、起動の遅さの問題は解決しない。

references.quote: The optional grace period to provide containers time to bootstrap in before failed health checks count towards the maximum number of retries.
You can specify between 1 and 10 retries.
You can specify between 5 and 300 seconds. The default value is 30 seconds.
You can specify between 2 and 60 seconds. The default value is 5 seconds.

questions.stem_en: An Amazon ECS task has an application container and a log-forwarding sidecar container. The essential parameter is omitted for both. When the sidecar crashes, the whole task stops. The team wants the sidecar's failure to leave the application running, and wants the task's health to reflect only whether the application is healthy. Which actions should the team take? (Choose TWO.)

choices_en.text: Set essential to false for the sidecar container.
Define a health check command for the application container, and keep it essential.
Set essential to false for both containers.
Add a health check command to the sidecar and keep it essential so that its health is reported too.
Keep the essential parameter omitted for the sidecar, because omitted means non-essential.

explanation.summary: essential が true のコンテナが止まると、タスクの他のコンテナも全て止まる。false なら他に影響しない。省くと essential とみなされ、タスクには少なくとも 1 つの essential のコンテナが要る。タスクの健全性は、essential でヘルスチェックのコマンドを持つコンテナだけで決まる。

per_choice.A: 正しい。サイドカーが止まってもアプリは動き続ける。
per_choice.B: 正しい。essential でヘルスチェックを持つアプリのコンテナだけで、タスクの健全性が決まる。
per_choice.C: タスクには少なくとも 1 つの essential のコンテナが要る。
per_choice.D: サイドカーの状態もタスクの健全性に入り、止まればタスクも止まる。
per_choice.E: 省くと essential とみなされる。

references.quote: If this parameter is omitted, a container is assumed to be essential.
If the essential parameter of a container is marked as false, then its failure doesn't affect the rest of the containers in a task.
All tasks must have at least one essential container.
Containers that are essential and have health check command in the task definition are the only ones considered to determine the task health.

questions.stem_en: An AWS CodeDeploy deployment to Amazon EC2 instances runs a script in the ValidateService hook that polls the application until it returns healthy responses, which can take up to 4 minutes. The hook's timeout is set to 60 seconds, and deployments fail at ValidateService even when the application becomes healthy. The team must keep verifying the deployment before it is marked successful. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices_en.text: Increase the timeout of the ValidateService hook to 7200 seconds.
Move the polling script to the BeforeInstall hook.
Remove the ValidateService hook so that deployments complete without the check.
Increase the timeout of the ValidateService hook to 300 seconds.

explanation.summary: hooks の timeout は、スクリプトが失敗とみなされるまでの秒数で、既定と最大は 3600 秒（1 時間）。超えるとデプロイが止まり、そのインスタンスへのデプロイは失敗する。ValidateService は最後のライフサイクルイベントで、デプロイがうまく終わったかを確かめるのに使う。

per_choice.A: 1 つのライフサイクルイベントのスクリプトに許されるのは最大 3600 秒。
per_choice.B: BeforeInstall はアプリを入れる前で、入れた後の確かめにならない。
per_choice.C: 成功とする前に確かめる要件に反する。
per_choice.D: 正しい。4 分の確かめが収まる長さにする。

references.quote: The number of seconds to allow the script to execute before it is considered to have failed. The default is 3600 seconds (1 hour).
3600 seconds (1 hour) is the maximum amount of time allowed for script execution for each deployment lifecycle event.
ValidateService – This is the last deployment lifecycle event. It is used to verify the deployment was completed successfully.
